query: Someone spread a false statement to damage my reputation. What offence may apply?

phase8.query: Someone spread a false statement to damage my reputation. What offence may apply?

variants.query: Someone spread a false statement to damage my reputation. What offence may apply?

original.chapter_title: OF CRIMINAL INTIMIDATION, INSULT, ANNOYANCE, DEFAMATION, ETC.
original.text: It does not amount to an offence, within the meaning of this section, when the person making, publishing or circulating any such statement, false information, rumor or report, has reasonable grounds for believing that such statement, false information, rumor or report is true and makes, publishes or circulates it in good faith and without any such intent as aforesaid. Act caused by inducing person to believe that he will be rendered an object of Divine displeasure.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 19: OF CRIMINAL INTIMIDATION, INSULT, ANNOYANCE, DEFAMATION, ETC.
Section 353: Statements conducing to public mischief.
Whoever commits an offence specified in sub-section (2) in any place of worship or in any assembly engaged in the performance of religious worship or religious ceremonies, shall be punished with imprisonment which may extend to five years and shall also be liable to fine.
It does not amount to an offence, within the meaning of this section, when the person making, publishing or circulating any such statement, false information, rumor or report, has reasonable grounds for believing that such statement, false information, rumor or report is true and makes, publishes or circulates it in good faith and without any such intent as aforesaid. Act caused by inducing person to believe that he will be rendered an object of Divine displeasure.

original.chapter_title: OF CRIMINAL INTIMIDATION, INSULT, ANNOYANCE, DEFAMATION, ETC.
original.text: A person who makes a speech in public, submits that speech to the judgment of the public.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 19: OF CRIMINAL INTIMIDATION, INSULT, ANNOYANCE, DEFAMATION, ETC.
Section 356: Defamation.
Whoever, by words either spoken or intended to be read, or by signs or by visible representations, makes or publishes in any manner, any imputation concerning any person intending to harm, or knowing or having reason to believe that such imputation will harm, the reputation of such person, is said, except in the cases hereinafter excepted, to defame that person.
A person who makes a speech in public, submits that speech to the judgment of the public.

original.chapter_title: OF CRIMINAL INTIMIDATION, INSULT, ANNOYANCE, DEFAMATION, ETC.
original.text: An imputation in the form of an alternative or expressed ironically, may amount to defamation.

An imputation in the form of an alternative or expressed ironically, may amount to defamation.

original.chapter_title: OF CRIMINAL INTIMIDATION, INSULT, ANNOYANCE, DEFAMATION, ETC.
original.text: It may amount to defamation to impute anything to a deceased person, if the imputation would harm the reputation of that person if living, and is intended to be hurtful to the feelings of his family or other near relatives.

original.chapter_title: OF FALSE EVIDENCE AND OFFENCES AGAINST PUBLIC JUSTICE
original.text: Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause that person to give false evidence shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.

phase11.final_answer: Defamation may apply if a false statement is made with intent to damage reputation, as per Section 353(1) and Section 356(1) Explanation 3 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.
phase11.summary_answer: The offence of defamation may apply if someone spreads a false statement to damage your reputation.
phase11.detailed_answer: According to Section 353(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, making, publishing, or circulating any false statement or information can constitute an offence. If the statement is made with the intent to harm someone's reputation, it may be classified as defamation. However, if the person spreading the statement has reasonable grounds to believe it is true and acts in good faith, it may not amount to an offence as per Section 353(3) Exception. Additionally, Section 356(1) Explanation 3 indicates that certain forms of imputation, even if expressed ironically, can also be considered defamation. Therefore, if the false statement was made without reasonable belief in its truth and with intent to harm, it could lead to legal consequences.

llm_evidence.chapter_title: OF FALSE EVIDENCE AND OFFENCES AGAINST PUBLIC JUSTICE
llm_evidence.text: Whoever threatens another with any injury to his person, reputation or property or to the person or reputation of any one in whom that person is interested, with intent to cause that person to give false evidence shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both.
